confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'Because this involves an active earth fault and potential fire risk' and 'The boil-overs are very likely the cause' - stated as fact without knowing which device trips; overload of an MCB (two zones on high plus kettle) was never considered or asked about

rationale: Safety handling was sound: stop-use, isolate at the consumer unit, no live tests, and referral to an electrician or appliance engineer, with the faint electrical smell correctly treated as a reason not to run it again. It used the customer's boil-over and two-zones-on-high evidence and recommended no parts. However it never asked the key question of which switch trips (RCD vs MCB), and it declared 'an active earth fault' as fact when the evidence is equally consistent with overload or a circuit issue, so calibration is weaker than the ground truth warrants. A UK homeowner would still be reasonably served, ending with a safe, correct escalation.
